short: An Athenian statesman whose leadership initiated the golden age of classical Athens.
full:
Pericles was a prominent and influential Greek statesman, orator, and general of Athens during its golden age, specifically the time between the Persian and Peloponnesian wars. He was descended from the powerful Alcmaeonid family and became the principal figure in Athenian politics. His policies transformed the Delian League into an Athenian empire and fostered a period of profound cultural and intellectual brilliance.

Under Pericles, Athens saw the construction of the Parthenon and other major structures on the Acropolis, which served to glorify the city and employ its citizens. He also promoted the arts and literature, making Athens the educational and cultural centre of the ancient Greek world. His democratic reforms expanded the participation of poorer citizens in politics, though his ambitious foreign policies eventually led Athens into the devastating Peloponnesian War against Sparta, during which he succumbed to the Plague of Athens.
